office.name: Office of State Representative Marla Brockhoff, Kansas House District 13
office.place: Kansas House District 13 (Chase, Greenwood, Woodson and Wilson counties and southwest Lyon County, including the southwest corner of Emporia); district office in Eureka, Kansas
office.district_office: 118 W. Second St., Eureka, KS 67045 (rented storefront, opened Sept 21, 2026); (620) 583-4130
office.capitol_office: Room 151-S, Kansas Statehouse, Topeka (staffed by a session legislative assistant January-May only)
office.remit: A part-time citizen legislator in the 125-member Kansas House. The Legislature is in its interim (no session) from June to January; interim committees meet in Topeka. The office answers constituent mail, helps constituents with state agencies (KanCare, KDOL unemployment, KDOR, KDOT, licensing boards), tracks bills and interim committee work, and publishes a newsletter. It has no authority over state agencies, counties or cities. Kansas pays legislators a salary and a postage and newsletter printing allotment (LCC Policy 38) but no district office or district staff allowance; this office's rent and staff are paid from the representative's officeholder account (campaign funds may be used for 'expenses of holding political office', K.S.A. 25-4157a).

official.title: Representative
official.party: Republican (chosen by the Republican district convention; the real seat is Republican-held). Not stated anywhere in the prompt or drive.
official.background: Fourth-generation cattle rancher near Cottonwood Falls (Chase County); runs the family ranch company, Brockhoff Land & Cattle LLC, with her husband Dean. Former 4-H leader and county extension council member. First public office.
official.took_office_sentence: was chosen by a district convention of precinct committee members and appointed by the governor in September 2026 after the previous representative resigned
official.next_election_sentence: the seat is on the November 3 ballot

succession.rule: K.S.A. 25-3902: when a state representative's seat falls vacant, the party county chairperson calls a convention of the party's precinct committeemen and committeewomen in the district within 21 days of notice (at least 10 days' notice for a multi-county district); the convention elects a person, and the governor appoints that person within seven days of receiving the certificate (if the governor fails to act, the person is deemed appointed). The appointee serves the rest of the term (to January 2027).
succession.nomination: The previous representative was also the November 2026 nominee and withdrew from the nomination on Sept 1 (K.S.A. 25-306b allows withdrawal on or before Sept 1 after the primary); the vacancy in the party nomination is filled by the party under K.S.A. 25-3904/25-3905. The same Sept 12 convention chose Brockhoff for both, so she is the nominee on the Nov 3 ballot.
succession.timeline: Sept 1 (Tue) resignation effective and withdrawal from the nomination; Sept 12 (Sat) district convention in Eureka; Sept 14 (Mon) certificate to the governor; Sept 18 (Fri) governor's appointment; Sept 21 (Mon) oath of office, Chase County Courthouse, Cottonwood Falls; district office opens the same afternoon.
sources: http://www.ksrevisor.gov/docs/LCC_Packet20260108/Item_2_LCC_Policy_38_Amend.pdf (LCC Policy 38, as amended Jan 8, 2026: $6,000 representative allotment; not usable after May 31 in a general election year)
